body.x: Robros (CEO Ryan Ro) participated on January 6 (local time) at the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026, a venue that brings together “Korean-style humanoid” technologies in a single space.

Robros is a Korean company that has built specialized expertise in humanoid robotics. It is developing robots equipped with precision control actuators, intuitive human–robot interaction (HRI) design, and proprietary algorithms that enable real-time motion prediction and situational adaptation.

The company has secured a full-cycle technology stack spanning mechanical design, system integration, assembly and production, control software, and AI. Based on this foundation, Robros currently offers solutions for research and exhibition purposes, while progressively advancing each technology component to realize platforms applicable to diverse industrial environments.

At CES 2026, Robros unveiled its flagship humanoid platform, IGRIS-C, representing the company’s core humanoid capabilities. The mid-size humanoid stands 154 cm tall and weighs 60 kg, and is designed with a total of 31 degrees of freedom (DoF) across the body, excluding the hands, to enable precise, expressive movement.

Each hand employs a tendon-driven structure in which actuators and joints are connected via wires, delivering 6 active DoF per hand. Including passive degrees of freedom, each hand reaches a total of 11 DoF. The lightweight robot hands, each weighing approximately 300 grams, can handle payloads of up to 3 kg per hand, providing sufficient performance for manipulating a wide range of everyday objects.

body.cap: Robros booth at the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: For actuation, IGRIS-C adopts low-reduction-ratio (20:1 or less) QDD actuators to enhance joint compliance. The knee and hip pitch joints can deliver torque of up to 150 Nm. The walking mechanism was developed through reinforcement learning in a simulation environment, and the combination of extensive training and high mobility has enabled stable bipedal locomotion.
Notably, IGRIS-C won first place in the bipedal walking and static obstacle avoidance category at the 24th IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots held in late September.

A Robros representative said, “CES 2026 provides an excellent opportunity to introduce our humanoid robotics technology and the IGRIS-C platform to the global market. Until now, we have mainly supplied robots domestically for research, education, and exhibition, but through this event, we aim to explore international technical exchange and collaboration to concretize our future expansion plans.”

The representative added, “By leveraging CES, where global attention is focused on advanced technologies including robotics and AI, we plan to gather feedback on the technical standards and operational environments demanded by the global market and reflect this in our technology development and business strategy. Through this process, we aim to accelerate the accumulation of technical stability and operational experience and pursue exports primarily to universities and research institutes in North America and Europe.”

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
